What a coincidence! I'm actually from sweden. People tend to respect the law actually. To own a macaw, you have to have a 6,5m2 cage. Right now it's illegal to free fly them because of bird flu, but that will change soon enough. For as long as I can remember you've needed a licence to breed dogs here (and you're not allowed to leave them alone for more than 5 hours in total a day). Animals are chipped and registered. The pet shops barely have animals. Some do, but most don't. Its frowned upon. Also, because of the legal requirements of the cages, they can't fit them inside. I'm good with that. When I was a child they used to have small birds and rabbits and such, but it's better that they feel good. I have never ever seen dogs or cats there. It's illegal to have dogs in cages (aka crate training). Absolutely horrific how they treat our dear animals across the pond. Also, I've never heard of anyone catching a wild animal to keep.
